lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Experience is not in newest-first order because Crestline appears above the more recent Harbor Payments role.
items.because: The ordering makes the sequence harder to follow and hides the more recent product internship.

items.says: The diesel mechanic entry takes space and prominence from the product internship and projects.
items.because: Its two bullets make the résumé’s product-management focus less immediate.

items.says: Education appears before Experience, so work and product evidence do not lead.
items.because: The education section precedes the experience that demonstrates applied work and product contributions.

items.says: The current-role bullet uses past tense instead of present tense.
The current-role bullet uses past tense instead of present tense.
The maintenance task and its result are not specified.
The scorecards and meeting are described as responsibilities, without an action or outcome.
items.because: The reader cannot tell what you did in the meeting or whether the work changed a decision or carrier performance.

items.says: The phrase about the monthly review is wordy and leaves your role vague.
items.because: It does not say whether you led or contributed to the review.

items.says: The driver-hour savings are buried after several rollout activities.
items.because: The reader encounters the activities before the operational payoff.

items.says: The line misdefines RICE Reach as support tickets closed.
items.because: Standard RICE Reach estimates the users or other units affected over a defined period; mislabeling it can change feature rankings.

items.says: The line does not name the roadmap decision the prioritization produced.
items.because: Without the selected initiative, the reader cannot see what the prioritization accomplished.

items.says: The selected roadmap priority is buried after the supporting analysis.
items.because: The long list of methods makes the product bet less visible.

items.says: A session-randomized test does not, by itself, establish a customer-level conversion effect.
items.because: Customers may have multiple sessions, so a session-weighted lift can differ from a lift among unique customers.

items.says: The bullet repeats the checkout test and conversion lift already reported earlier.
items.because: Reporting the same result again makes the achievement appear duplicated and uses space for another contribution.

items.says: The wording makes the leadership team, rather than the presentation, the grammatical subject of the funding result.
“That would have been thrown away” is wordy.
items.because: The longer phrase adds words without adding meaning to the result.

items.says: “With two dining halls” leaves the halls’ relationship to the app launch unclear.
The 400-to-1,150 increase is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: The increase of 750 users is 187.5% of the starting 400.

items.says: The wording does not make clear whether the interviews informed the reminders’ design.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: The relative increase is about 26.7%, so “20%” conflicts with the endpoints.

items.says: The $2.4M saving estimate has no stated baseline or key assumption.
The intake work is written in passive voice.
The line does not say how much the form was shortened or what the change improved.
The recommendation lacks the analysis or evidence that supported it.
The pilot approval repeats the outcome in the savings bullet.
items.because: Repeating the same approval or funding outcome takes space from the recommendation’s supporting evidence.
